deck.p2: “Short version: it’s a free grow journal, and there’s an optional crypto layer most users never touch. I’d rather you check the limits than take my word for it — so here they are first.”

deck.h2: What we claim, and what we don’t.
deck.p3: This slide comes first on purpose. If a claim you expected is missing from the left column, that’s deliberate.
deck.li: The journal, camera, illness check, and coach ship today — free, no wallet
deck.li2: Every mint is a real transaction you can open in a public explorer
deck.li3: Adopters see the same trail the grower sees
deck.li4: The architecture and the risks are published, not on request
deck.li5: That $GROWTOO has value — it’s a devnet test asset
deck.li6: Any yield, return, or financial outcome
deck.li7: That the system is trustless today
deck.li8: That harvest redemption works — it’s specified, not shipped
deck.li9: That growtoo is legal advice for your jurisdiction
deck.li14: That Check for illness is a lab diagnosis — it is a photo hypothesis
deck.h22: Who you have to trust right now.
deck.p4: The honest answer is: us, at one specific step. A grower could in principle write a journal entry that didn’t happen, so today the platform operator reviews progress before a stage is minted. Listing on Market also requires 14 days of saved care logs, so a same-night dump cannot go to the board. That is a single point of trust plus a time gate — we name both rather than hide them behind the word “on-chain”.
deck.p6: The trusted step. Today, that’s us
deck.p7: Immutable once written — not proof it was true
deck.p8: Public tx, linked to the entry
deck.p9: The chain proves what was recorded and when. It does not prove the plant was watered.
deck.p10: The roadmap is about removing ourselves from the middle of that review step, in the order that actually reduces risk rather than the order that sounds most decentralised.
deck.p11: In-app camera, illness checks, and journal entries. Market listing also needs 14 days of saved care logs — a one-night dump cannot go to the board.
deck.p12: More than one party signing that a stage happened, not just the operator.
deck.p13: A real fulfillment path, so a false claim has a consequence at harvest.
deck.p14: Current design and the intended path are written up in the architecture docs.
deck.h24: Don’t take the deck’s word for it.
deck.p15: Four real plants on Solana’s public test network. Open the transactions, check the timestamps, compare them against the journal in the app.
deck.div6: Sign up free, no wallet Read the risks page Read the architecture docs
deck.h25: The ways this could go wrong.
deck.p16: Listed because they’re real, not because a lawyer asked. Detail and mitigations live on the risks page.
deck.p17: Cultivation and redemption rules differ per country and can move against us.
deck.p18: Turning a harvest token into a physical counterpart is the hardest unsolved step.
deck.p19: Self-reported entries can be gamed; listing now requires elapsed time and 50% coverage so same-day farms fail. Still not a plant oracle.
deck.p20: Self-custody means a lost key is a lost token. No recovery on our side.
deck.p21: Today one party reviews mints. That’s a concentration risk until it isn’t.
deck.p22: Devnet balances aren’t transferable value. Migration rules publish before launch.
deck.h26: After all that — this part stands.
deck.p23: Strip out everything unproven and there’s still a working product that people use for free with no exposure to any of the above.
